title: doctor text output drops required provider evidence
description: docs/THREAT_MODEL.md trust boundary 2 states that doctor reports path, signature validity, identifier, and Apple anchor evidence. The human renderer in Sources/SSHCTLCore/CLI.swift prints only 'provider: verified|unverified', collapsing signatureValid and appleAnchored into one word and omitting path and identifier entirely. Only --json satisfies the documented invariant, so an operator reading the default output cannot tell an unsigned provider from a non-Apple-anchored one.
acceptance_criteria: doctor text output shows provider path, signature validity, Apple anchor, and identifier as separate signals; a test asserts each appears.
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove identity delete and Homebrew tap dispatch as breaking changes
description:
A two-axis code review of 7ab62f4...HEAD found two features shipped against explicit spec prohibitions:

1. 'identity delete' — HANDOFF.md said 'Defer destructive lifecycle commands until creation, discovery, wrapper handling, and verification are proven' and 'Do not add deletion in the same milestone.' The command shipped in v0.1.x anyway, and the prohibiting sentence was later deleted from HANDOFF.md rather than honoured.
2. Homebrew tap release automation (release.yml tap dispatch, docs/RELEASING.md) — HANDOFF.md said 'do not sign, notarize, install, publish, commit, or push releases.'

Both were legitimised by editing the spec after the fact, with no decision record.
design:
Revert both. The spec is the authority; the after-the-fact spec edits are withdrawn.

Removing shipped commands is a breaking change, which is acceptable and normal — it is announced in the release notes rather than avoided. Deletion in particular is the one irreversible operation in the tool: shipping it before the bio path, locked/logged-out/reboot/launchd contexts, and recovery workflows were hardware-verified inverted the spec's ordering, which existed to keep an unproven tool from destroying the only credential a user has.

Scope:
- delete IdentityDeleter, IdentityDeleteReport, 'identity delete' CLI routing and help, and the delete-specific IdentityLifecycleError cases
- delete the tap-token and tap-dispatch steps from .github/workflows/release.yml and the corresponding docs/RELEASING.md section; GitHub release publication stays
- restore the prohibiting sentences in HANDOFF.md and point them at this bead
- announce both removals as breaking in the next release notes
acceptance_criteria: identity delete is absent from the binary, help text, README, and tests; release.yml publishes a GitHub release and dispatches nothing; HANDOFF.md's deferral sentences are restored; the removals are written up as breaking changes for the next release.
notes: User decision on 2026-09-01 during code-review follow-up: 'breaking change로 잡고 release 노트에 명시', clarified as remove-and-announce. Re-adding deletion later is gated on the hardware verification listed in docs/HARDWARE_VERIFICATION.md.
close_reason: Closed

title: Keep external automation integration out of the CLI
description:
The originating HANDOFF.md spec (commit 7ab62f4) required a post-creation HTTPS webhook delivering ssh.key.created events, with nine constraints: HMAC request auth, bounded timeouts, deterministic JSON, idempotent eventId, no private material in payloads, partial-success state on delivery failure, a non-secret outbox for explicit retry, optional delivery tested against a local mock server, and a protocol-boundary sink so tests need no network.

None of it was implemented. Instead the whole section was deleted from HANDOFF.md and replaced with the opposite instruction: 'Keep external integration out of this CLI. It may print verified public-key metadata as human-readable text or schema-versioned JSON, but it must not deliver events, manage network credentials, persist delivery queues, or call automation services.'

A code review found this reversal had no recorded rationale, so the spec edit read as the requirement having never existed.
design:
Confirmed as the intended direction, not an oversight. The CLI stays a local, non-networking tool.

Rationale: a tool holding Secure Enclave identity authority should not also hold network credentials, an outbox, or retry state. Every added responsibility widens the blast radius of the one process allowed to request signatures. Emitting schema-versioned JSON on stdout lets any external automation do delivery with its own credentials and its own failure handling, outside this trust boundary.

Consequence: the ssh.key.created event contract, HMAC signing, and outbox retry are out of scope permanently, not deferred. Downstream automation consumes 'se-sshctl identity create --json' and 'se-sshctl install --json'.
notes: Recorded during the two-axis code review of 7ab62f4...HEAD (2026-09-01). HANDOFF.md was edited in commit range without this record; this bead is the missing rationale.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add repeatable MacBook Air Touch ID verification wizard
description: Promote the existing development-only bio probe into a reviewed, repeatable wizard. It must exercise current-source p-256-ne+bio creation, identity-file installation, local signing, optional isolated localhost authentication, exact cleanup, and append a truthful Markdown run record to docs/HARDWARE_VERIFICATION.md without persisting hashes, labels, passphrases, or key material.
acceptance_criteria: The committed wizard is linked from README/docs, uses the repository wizard template unchanged above STAGES, confirms destructive and authorized_keys mutations, restores local authorization byte-for-byte, deletes its test identity, appends only an explicit passed/not-run record, passes bash -n and shellcheck, and is not run automatically by the agent.

title: Support non-empty identity-file passphrases in remote verification
description: install explicitly supports a non-empty identity-file passphrase, but verify remote invokes ssh with BatchMode=yes and IdentityAgent=none. OpenSSH BatchMode disables passphrase prompting, so this verification path cannot unlock the encrypted identity file unless another mechanism is added or the feature is explicitly constrained. Reproduce on a physical supported Mac and align implementation, help, README, and tests.
acceptance_criteria: A passphrase-protected identity file produced by se-sshctl can complete verify remote on supported hardware without exposing the passphrase in argv, environment values, persistent files, or output; or install/help explicitly reject/document the unsupported combination. Add a runnable regression and physical-Mac evidence.
notes:
Code review of 7ab62f4...HEAD (2026-09-01) folded a second, related finding into this bead by user decision.

install is TTY-gated: Sources/se-sshctl/main.swift sets RPP_REQUIRE_TTY and CLI.swift throws 'install requires a controlling terminal for passphrase input' when no reader is supplied. That blocks HANDOFF.md verification-matrix item 6, 'non-interactive remote command execution', and sits close to the spec's forbidden 'TTY passphrase gate'. The caveat is documented only in docs/THREAT_MODEL.md — installHelp does not mention it.

The two findings are one problem seen from both ends: the passphrase can only be supplied interactively, and the paths that must consume it (verify local, verify remote) run non-interactively. Resolve them together rather than opening a non-interactive install path in isolation, which would widen the security surface without fixing verification. Any fix needs a threat-model update and physical-Mac evidence.

title: Verify -t none signing from remote session contexts on hardware
description:
The handoff's required test classes include 'none signing from remote session contexts'. It cannot be faked: it is about what the Secure Enclave actually does when the operator is connected over SSH with no attached GUI session, which is the primary use case the whole -t none path exists for.

docs/THREAT_MODEL.md already records the locked-console, logged-out, reboot-before-first-unlock, and launchd contexts as unverified. This is the same gap stated as the test the specification asked for.
acceptance_criteria: Physical-Mac evidence that a -t none identity signs and authenticates from an SSH session with the console locked, logged out, and after a reboot before first unlock; results appended to docs/HARDWARE_VERIFICATION.md, including any context where it does not work.

title: Persist a create-time verification manifest
description:
Verification outcomes are now tri-state and reported per run (se-sshctl-h3l), but nothing is written to disk. The handoff also requires a persisted manifest: 'A machine-readable manifest should include at least {...providerLoad/localSigning/remoteAuthentication: not-run}', and create-transaction step 12, 'Write the manifest only after state and fingerprint checks pass.'

Today an operator who ran verify local yesterday has no record of it; the next session starts from not-run with no way to distinguish 'never tested' from 'tested last week'. That is the same failure the tri-state work fixed, displaced in time.
design:
Open questions before implementing: where the manifest lives (alongside the identity file, or a per-user state directory), whether it is per-identity or a single inventory, what happens when it disagrees with the live CTK inventory, and whether a stale manifest entry decays back to not-run after some interval.

It must contain no private material and no passphrase, consistent with the identity file's own boundary, and writing it must not become a way to make an unverified identity look verified.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest is written only after state and fingerprint checks pass; it records providerLoad, localSigning, and remoteAuthentication with timestamps; a stale or conflicting manifest never reports as passed; its location and schema are documented.

title: verify remote captures no client diagnostics
description: HANDOFF.md: 'Capture client verbose logs and server authentication logs. Make the result part of verify remote diagnostics.' RemoteVerifier runs ssh without -v, and stderr surfaces only inside a commandFailed error string, so a failed remote verification gives the operator nothing to act on.
acceptance_criteria: verify remote runs ssh verbosely and carries the captured client log into its report and its failure output.
close_reason: Closed

title: Verification reports cannot express failed or not-run
description: HANDOFF.md requires a machine-readable manifest recording providerLoad, localSigning, and remoteAuthentication, and states: 'Represent passed, failed, and not-run separately. Never turn not tested into success.' VerificationReport hardcodes status = "passed" and is only ever constructed on the success path, so every check that did not run is indistinguishable from one that passed. Nothing is persisted, so create-transaction step 12 (write the manifest only after state and fingerprint checks pass) has no implementation.
acceptance_criteria: verification status is a tri-state (passed/failed/not-run); reports name each check separately; a failing check produces a report rather than only an error.
close_reason: Tri-state passed/failed/not-run implemented and reported per run; the persisted create-time manifest split to se-sshctl-0o5.

title: Split OperationalCommands.swift and de-duplicate the verifiers
description: OperationalCommands.swift is 451 lines covering identity-file install, SSH config rendering, local verification, and remote verification — four unrelated reasons to change one file. LocalVerifier.verify and RemoteVerifier.verify additionally share about twenty near-identical lines (normalize hash, validate path, require .pub, require trusted provider, resolve identity, run ssh-keygen -l, compare fingerprint); the fingerprint comparison appears a third time in IdentityFileInstaller. ResolvedIdentity.providerHash is also misnamed: it holds the CTK SHA-1/hex hash that CONTEXT.md calls the sc_auth deletion and provider-selection locator.
acceptance_criteria: install, config rendering, and verification live in separate files; the shared verification preflight exists once; providerHash is renamed to match CONTEXT.md.
close_reason: Closed

title: Give Protection and key type their own types
description: CONTEXT.md names Protection a first-class concept with exactly two values (bio, none), but it travels as a bare String. It is validated by ["bio", "none"].contains(...) in both CTKIdentityParser and IdentityCreator.create, then re-switched as 'protection == "bio" ? 120 : 30' and 'protection == "bio" ? Data() : Data("0".utf8)'. Key type is the same shape: a String checked against a five-element list in the parser and against "p-256-ne" in the creator.
acceptance_criteria: Protection and key type are enums decoded once at the parser boundary; the repeated membership checks and value switches are gone.
close_reason: Closed

title: Collapse duplicated subprocess success checks
description: The predicate 'guard !result.timedOut, result.terminationReason == .exit, result.exitStatus == 0' is written out seven times across ReadOnlyCommands.swift (four, including both ProviderInspector closures), LifecycleCommands.requireSuccess, and OperationalCommands.requireOperationalSuccess. A single computed property on SubprocessResult collapses all of them and keeps the definition of success in one place.

The same file also carries wizard-template functions this script never calls (ask, ask_secret, write_env, set_secret, set_var, open_url) plus ENV_FILE/WRITTEN_ENV/WRITTEN_SECRET state, and invokes system_profiler SPHardwareDataType three times where one capture suffices.

title: se-sshctl exists as safety porcelain over Apple CTK and OpenSSH
description:
Decision: retain se-sshctl as a narrow safety-focused orchestration layer over Apple system tools, not as a cryptographic implementation, SSH agent, or remote authorization manager. Its product value is deterministic identity selection, fail-closed lifecycle postconditions, collision-safe identity-file installation, secret-safe prompt mediation, trusted-provider checks, and isolated signing/authentication verification beyond the native single-identity recipe.

Consequences:
- README must state this value directly and distinguish orchestration from cryptographic novelty.
- Prefer stronger hardware evidence and compatibility validation over broader feature scope.
- Remote authorization, CA/KRL workflows, backup, migration, and GUI management remain outside the project unless separately justified.
- If Apple fixes the native selection and verification gaps so this layer no longer removes meaningful operator complexity, reevaluate whether the project should continue.
close_reason: Accepted and reflected in README positioning and the hardware-evidence workflow.

title: Assess whether se-sshctl adds value beyond the HN recipe
description: Compare README claims, the HN/native command recipe, implementation, tests, threat model, and hardware evidence. Determine whether the project is merely a Swift wrapper or earns its existence through independent correctness, security, or operational value. Deliver a candid evidence-based assessment without code changes.
notes: Verdict: conditional yes. The project is a native-tool orchestration layer, not a new cryptographic implementation. Its defensible value is deterministic, fail-closed handling of CTK/OpenSSH quirks: strict identity parsing, exact SHA-256 selection across native hash domains, multi-identity collision-safe identity-file installation, secret-safe prompt mediation, provider checks, isolated local/remote verification, and post-delete checks. Convenience value is modest because the happy path remains as long as the HN recipe and remote authorization/config edits remain manual. Maturity is early: repository is one day old, current evidence covers only macOS 26.6.1/OpenSSH 10.3p1 with p-256-ne+none, bio/session contexts and OS matrix remain open, and non-empty identity-file passphrases conflict with BatchMode remote verification (se-sshctl-691). Overall: worth existing as narrow safety porcelain, not yet justified as a broadly production-ready Secure Enclave SSH manager.
close_reason: Completed evidence-based existence/value assessment; filed se-sshctl-691 for the passphrase verification gap.

notes:
MacBook Air bio wizard reproduced wrapper-install timeout with empty wrapper passphrase. Root cause in v0.1.0: download input always sent provider PIN 0; bio requires an empty provider PIN. Added protection-aware input and explicit timeout diagnostics; unit regression and full suite pass. Awaiting patched bottle rerun on physical Touch ID hardware.
Physical Mac differential confirmed: direct TTY ssh-keygen -K succeeds and downloads resident wrappers without a Touch ID prompt, while v0.1.1 wrapper install hangs after CLI passphrase capture. Root cause: OpenSSH readpassphrase prefers the controlling /dev/tty over piped stdin; buffered PIN/passphrase input is therefore not consumed. Implemented forced SSH_ASKPASS with a private in-memory FIFO so secrets are absent from argv, environment values, and disk; overwrite answers remain on stdin. Awaiting v0.1.2 bottle hardware rerun.
v0.1.2 physical-Mac run proved the FIFO/shell workaround functional, but independent security review rejected it: inherited shell xtrace could disclose passphrases and an orphan askpass process could hold stderr past timeout. Replaced the workaround in the working tree with native se-sshctl self-exec askpass: each invocation consumes exactly one bounded line from the existing anonymous stdin pipe; no shell, FIFO, argv secret, environment-value secret, or persistent secret file. Unexpected prompts fail immediately at EOF. Added empty/non-empty, EOF, exact-one-line, timeout, and multi-identity overwrite-position regressions. Full 34-test suite, release build, native entry-point probe, xtrace non-disclosure check, and git diff --check pass. Awaiting a new bottle and physical Touch ID rerun before claiming hardware verification.
Independent Claude Code security/spec review of 8ffd9ac found a conditional prompt-order flaw: if OpenSSH omitted the PIN prompt, fixed untagged replies could shift and silently create an empty-passphrase wrapper; it also flagged SIGTERM-only timeout handling. Follow-up fix tags PIN/passphrase replies, validates each OpenSSH prompt, requires exactly two non-secret passphrase success markers, rejects unknown/extra prompts even if ssh-keygen exits 0, and escalates timeout from SIGTERM to SIGKILL. Native OpenSSH integration reproduced PIN omission with a regular ed25519 key and now succeeds with the requested non-empty passphrase; full 37-test suite, release build, and xtrace non-disclosure check pass. verify-bio.sh is explicitly gitignored and remains a development-only hardware probe.
Claude follow-up review confirmed prompt-shift and direct-child timeout fixes, then identified one remaining medium: an ssh-sk-helper descendant could keep stdout/stderr pipes open after the direct ssh-keygen child died. ProcessExecutor now recursively enumerates its macOS child process tree with proc_listchildpids and kills descendants on timeout before SIGTERM/SIGKILL handling the direct child. A resistant ProxyCommand descendant regression (ignores HUP/TERM and sleeps) returns in 0.14s. Missing/extra passphrase success markers are also fail-closed; full suite is now 38 passing tests and release build passes.
Published v0.1.3 at fda05b1. Source release run 31513337041, tap formula test run 31513423440, and bottle publish run 31513725369 all succeeded. Committed-path preparation completed in working tree: scripts/verify-bio.sh now builds current source on a physical MacBook Air, verifies p-256-ne+bio creation/install/local signing, optionally probes isolated localhost authentication with byte-for-byte authorized_keys restoration, deletes the exact test identity, and offers to append a non-secret Markdown run to docs/HARDWARE_VERIFICATION.md. README and hardware docs link the wizard. Static bash syntax, shellcheck, full 37-test suite, release build, doctor JSON, and diff checks pass. The wizard was intentionally not run by the agent; physical Touch ID evidence remains required before closing this parent issue.

2026-08-12 hardware rerun attempt was blocked safely at verify-bio.sh stage 1: the active execution host identifies as Mac Studio (Mac13,2, Apple M1 Ultra), not MacBook Air. The wizard exited before Touch ID enrollment confirmation, CTK identity creation, authorized_keys mutation, or documentation append, so there was nothing to clean up. bash -n, shellcheck, all 37 Swift tests, release build, and git diff --check pass. docs/HARDWARE_VERIFICATION.md still contains only the pre-existing wizard documentation diff and no new hardware run or sensitive run data. The wizard restored ~/.ssh/authorized_keys byte-for-byte; an independent before/after SHA-256 and mode/owner/group/size comparison also matched. The exact run-created CTK identity was deleted and its run label is absent from identity list; two older pre-existing se-sshctl-bio identities remain untouched. title: Plumbing preserves native security-tool vocabulary
description:
# Plumbing preserves native security-tool vocabulary

`se-sshctl` separates low-level plumbing from policy-bearing porcelain. When a plumbing input represents a `sc_auth`, `ssh-keygen`, or SSH parameter, it keeps the native option name and value vocabulary instead of translating it into deployment-specific profiles; porcelain may compose those primitives for user-defined workflows without changing plumbing semantics.

## Consequences

- Plumbing may validate the SSH-only scope, fix trusted executable/provider paths, require destructive or unattended-signing acknowledgement, and verify postconditions. These are safety invariants, not deployment policy.
- Plumbing does not have to expose every native flag. A deep command may hide several native calls, but any native concept it does expose keeps the native spelling and semantics.
- Native identifiers remain distinct: `sc_auth delete-ctk-identity -h` consumes a SHA-1 CTK public-key hash, operational selection uses a SHA-256 CTK public-key hash, and wrapper matching uses an SSH fingerprint.
- Remote revocation and recovery checks belong to porcelain retirement, not the native delete primitive. External delivery, webhooks, and remote authorization mutation remain outside this CLI.
notes: Migrated from docs/adr/0001-plumbing-preserves-native-vocabulary.md; Beads decisions are now the architectural decision source of truth. Amended by se-sshctl-046: the public delete interface exposes CTK SHA-256 only, resolves native SHA-1 internally, and has no retirement command. Public OpenSSH file terminology was aligned by se-sshctl-xpa: install and --identity-file replace the former project-specific wrapper vocabulary.
close_reason: Accepted; migrated from the repository ADR document.
